symbols.name: index tuple
symbols.meaning: The tuple of indices (j_1,...,j_d), one per axis, locating an entry of an array.
symbols.quote: Data are arrays indexed by $\boldsymbol j=(j_1,\dots,j_d)$, where $d$ is the number of axes.

symbols.name: axis lengths
symbols.meaning: The tuple (t_1,...,t_d) of axis lengths, where t_i is the even number of entries along axis i.
symbols.quote: The tuple $\boldsymbol t=(t_1,\dots,t_d)$ lists the axis lengths, where $t_i$ is the even number of entries along axis $i$, and $s_i$ is an integer coprime to $t_i$.

symbols.name: coprime multiplier
symbols.meaning: An integer coprime to the axis length t_i.
symbols.quote: The tuple $\boldsymbol t=(t_1,\dots,t_d)$ lists the axis lengths, where $t_i$ is the even number of entries along axis $i$, and $s_i$ is an integer coprime to $t_i$.

symbols.name: normalized transform
symbols.meaning: The normalized multidimensional discrete Fourier transform with axis lengths t.
symbols.quote: The normalized transform $F_{\boldsymbol t}$ is given by $(F_{\boldsymbol t}u)_{\boldsymbol f}=\frac1T\sum_{\boldsymbol k}u_{\boldsymbol k}\exp(-2\pi i\sum_i k_if_i/t_i)$, where $\boldsymbol k$ runs over input positions and $\boldsymbol f=(f_1,\dots,f_d)$ is the frequency labelling an output entry.

symbols.name: input position
symbols.meaning: The index tuple of an input entry.
symbols.quote: The normalized transform $F_{\boldsymbol t}$ is given by $(F_{\boldsymbol t}u)_{\boldsymbol f}=\frac1T\sum_{\boldsymbol k}u_{\boldsymbol k}\exp(-2\pi i\sum_i k_if_i/t_i)$, where $\boldsymbol k$ runs over input positions and $\boldsymbol f=(f_1,\dots,f_d)$ is the frequency labelling an output entry.

symbols.name: frequency
symbols.meaning: The tuple of frequencies labelling an output entry of the transform.
symbols.quote: The normalized transform $F_{\boldsymbol t}$ is given by $(F_{\boldsymbol t}u)_{\boldsymbol f}=\frac1T\sum_{\boldsymbol k}u_{\boldsymbol k}\exp(-2\pi i\sum_i k_if_i/t_i)$, where $\boldsymbol k$ runs over input positions and $\boldsymbol f=(f_1,\dots,f_d)$ is the frequency labelling an output entry.

symbols.name: target permutation
symbols.meaning: The permutation reordering the output so that position j holds the entry of frequency (-s_i j_i)_i.
symbols.quote: The target permutation $Q$ reorders the output so that position $\boldsymbol j$ holds the entry of frequency $(-s_ij_i)_i$.

symbols.name: chirp
symbols.meaning: The chirp, a phase quadratic in the index.
symbols.quote: Define the chirp $a_{\boldsymbol j}=\exp\left(-\pi i\sum_{i=1}^d s_ij_i^2/t_i\right)$, a phase quadratic in the index, and let $\overline a$ be its complex conjugate.

relations.quote: The Bluestein chirp identity rewrites a permuted [Discrete Fourier transform](dft.md) as a pointwise chirp phase, a cyclic convolution, and another chirp phase, so the target permutation of resampling is absorbed into the convolution and never executed as a sort.
The permuted transform is thus reduced to one [Cyclic convolution](convolution.md) of length $T$ between two pointwise phase multiplications.

derivations.quote: Define the chirp $a_{\boldsymbol j}=\exp\left(-\pi i\sum_{i=1}^d s_ij_i^2/t_i\right)$, a phase quadratic in the index, and let $\overline a$ be its complex conjugate.

Replacing $j_i$ by $j_i+t_i$ changes the exponent by $-\pi i s_i\frac{(j_i+t_i)^2-j_i^2}{t_i}=-\pi i s_i(2j_i+t_i)$, which is an integral multiple of $2\pi i$ because $t_i$ is even, so $a$ has period $t_i$ in coordinate $i$.

Using $(j_i-k_i)^2=j_i^2-2j_ik_i+k_i^2$, the exponent of this product is $\sum_i\frac{\pi i s_i}{t_i}\bigl(j_i^2-(j_i^2-2j_ik_i+k_i^2)+k_i^2\bigr)$, where the squares cancel, so the coefficient is $\frac1T\overline a_{\boldsymbol j}a_{\boldsymbol j-\boldsymbol k}\overline a_{\boldsymbol k}=\frac1T\exp(2\pi i\sum_is_ij_ik_i/t_i)$.
This is precisely the coefficient of $QF_{\boldsymbol t}$ found above, because $Q$ reads frequency $(-s_ij_i)_i$ from the negative-sign transform.
